description.summary: push the logged-in user's settings to a shared compositor

protocol.description:
In the persistent-compositor model the compositor runs as its own system user and outlives every session, so it never sees the config of whoever is logged in: it reads its own, and nothing the user changes reaches it.
This protocol lets the logged-in user's session push settings in. The compositor stores what it receives in its own configuration and applies it through the same path as a local change, so senders need no access to the compositor's files and the compositor needs none to theirs.
The global is advertised ONLY to clients owned by the user whose session currently holds the screen. A client of any other user never sees it, so one user cannot reconfigure another's session, and it disappears at logout.

interface.name: agentos_session_config_v1

description.summary: settings channel for the active session

interface.description:
Pushes settings for the sending user's session.
A sender should push everything it manages once after binding, then a single entry whenever a value changes. The compositor keeps the last value it received for each entry until the session ends, at which point it returns to its own defaults.

request.name: set_entry
request.description:
Sets one entry, replacing any previous value for the same domain and key. The value is the serialized form the domain already uses on disk, so senders can forward what they read without re-encoding it.
An unknown domain, or a value the compositor cannot parse, is ignored: the compositor keeps its current value rather than falling back to a default, so a malformed push cannot disturb a working session.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the object. Entries already applied stay in effect for the rest of the session; the compositor discards them when the session ends.
